name: Chain of Custody
oneLine: Three claims hung from one reference standard as three little ladders — one whose top rung is a gold-jawed checkable source, one whose top rung is honestly hatched out, and one that hangs from nothing at all because it is a proficiency bar.
threeSecondRead: A calibration card is a claim with a chain above it: something independent it was checked against.
Here, one row's chain ends in gold at ANZ; one row's chain is broken at the top and says so; that is what the table below is.
The third specimen is the bar every other portfolio draws, and it visibly hangs from nothing — no source, no reading, two printed dashes.
form:
Pure HTML/CSS. No SVG, no `<path>`, so TC-BENCH-01/02 (`#skills svg path` = 20) are untouched. Styles in a new `CalibrationChain.module.css`, so TC-NFR-DEADCSS is out of scope.

APEX. Full `.inner` width. Mono 0.6rem/0.16em uppercase `--mist-400` label `REFERENCE STANDARD`, right-aligned on the same baseline `<Caliper state="self-reported">Vik_Resume_Final.pdf · MD5 16b856c0</Caliper>` (mono 0.68rem, `--white`; grey jaws + ◐ — his own document, correctly graded). Under it a 1px rule `--mist-200` @0.55 spanning grid columns 1–2 only; over column 3 the same 1px rule is dashed (`repeating-linear-gradient(to right, var(--mist-400) 0 3px, transparent 3px 6px)`, opacity .3) — Caliper's own 3/6 dash pitch. Sub-line mono 0.62rem `--mist-400`: `md5sum public/docs/Vik_Resume_Final.pdf · 157,615 bytes`.

COLUMNS. `grid-template-columns: repeat(3,1fr); gap: clamp(1.5rem,3.2vw,2.75rem)`. Each is a ladder: a 1px vertical stile at `left:0` in `--ink-500`, fed by a 26px drop from the apex, with three rungs. Rung = 14px×1px horizontal tick off the stile (`--mist-400`), label indented 1.35rem: mono 0.56rem/0.18em `--ink-400` (`R1 · STANDARD`, `R2 · READING`, `R3 · RESULT`), value below, sub-line below that. Rung labels align across all three columns — the comparison is automatic (device #18, small multiples).

Col 1 `TRACEABLE`: R1 `<Caliper state="sourced">ANZ Banking Group</Caliper>`, tick lengthened to 22px (major graduation, device #7); sub `programme · verified by asking the employer`. R2 mono 0.74rem tabular-nums `--white`: `10,000+ concurrent devices held at P95 under 200 ms`. R3 `--font-heading` 0.98rem: `Real-time telemetry platforms` + `● measured in production`.

Col 2 `LIMITED CALIBRATION` (UKAS LAB 5 §4.2's real term): R1 `<Caliper state="open">no certificate issued</Caliper>` — dashed jaws over 45° hatch; sub `credential · no issuing body yet`. Its stile *below R1* turns dashed for the whole drop — everything hanging below a broken link is not traceable, drawn. R3 `AWS and GCP certification` + `○ in progress, not yet held`.

Col 3 `NOT TRACEABLE` / `the device this card replaces`: R1 `–`, R2 `–` (printed en-dashes, `--mist-400` — metrology prints N/A, never blanks). R3 is the same claim string as col 1, verbatim, under a bar: 100%×8px track `--ink-500`, fill `--mist-400` to 78% with a dashed right edge, no percentage printed. Its stile is 14px and stops. Sub: `the end of this bar was chosen by the person drawing it.`

Gold appears exactly once: col 1 R1's caliper jaws.
motion: Three beats, 900 ms total, rules and ticks only — no text ever animates, so nothing is unreadable at any frame. Trigger: the exact one-shot `IntersectionObserver` from `Bench.tsx:194–206` (`threshold: 0.15`, `observer.disconnect()` on first hit), flipping `drawn`; a 940 ms timer flips `settled`, which sets `animation: none` so a resize or re-render can never replay it. Beat 1 (0–260 ms): apex rule rules itself in, `clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0) → inset(0 0 0 0)`, 260 ms. Beat 2 (260–560 ms): the drops and stiles grow downward, `transform: scaleY(0) → 1`, `transform-origin: top`, 300 ms, stagger `calc(var(--i) * 40ms)` (i = 0,1,2). Column 3's stile is 14 px and stops — its brevity lands last and is the punchline. Beat 3 (480–900 ms): rung ticks extend, `transform: scaleX(0) → 1`, `transform-origin: left`, 180 ms, staggered 46 ms in ROW-major order (R1 across all three columns, then R2, then R3) so the eye is walked along the comparison rather than down one ladder. Easing throughout is a new token `--motion-ease-mechanical: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` added to `globals.css` — decelerating, non-overshooting, because a caliper that bounces is a broken caliper; `--motion-ease-emphasized` overshoots and is wrong for an instrument. `--motion-` is an approved TC-NFR-TOKEN prefix, so the new token passes. Compositor-only (`transform`, `opacity`) except one `clip-path` on a 1px-tall element, which is negligible paint and runs once. No `will-change` at all. Motion is authored as the enhancement: base CSS is the settled frame, animations live inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, so a missed selector fails static, never animated.
states:
Reduced motion: `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` early-returns with `drawn = true` (the Bench pattern), and because motion is additive the settled frame is the base stylesheet — all three ladders complete at first paint. Identical for no-JS: the whole figure is server-rendered markup with no measurement, no ResizeObserver, no `getBoundingClientRect`, so the static export is complete without hydration. Zero canvas, so TC-CINE-04 passes; the h2 is untouched, so TC-CINE-07 passes.

390px: at `max-width: 860px` (the table's own breakpoint) the grid drops to `1fr` and the three ladders stack. Each column then carries its own top rule — solid above cols 1–2, dashed above col 3 — so the break survives the stack. Rung blocks become a `5.5rem 1fr` mini-grid so `R1 · STANDARD` sits beside its value and the three R1 rows remain scannable at ~40px each. Stiles and ticks are unchanged (1px and 14px are size-independent). Height ≈ 620px, which is affordable because the Bench has already collapsed to chips below 900px. An honest narrow-viewport strap prints under the figcaption at this breakpoint: `three specimens, stacked — compare the STANDARD rung of each.`

Keyboard: nothing focusable is added. The figure is entirely static — there is nothing to operate, so it adds no focus stops and cannot break the section's tab order or TC-SKILL-06's ±1px filter round-trip (it does not respond to the filters and its height is fixed).

Screen reader: `<figure aria-labelledby="chain-cap">` with a real `<figcaption>`. Every rule, tick, stile and drop is an `aria-hidden="true"` decorative `<span>`. The three `<Caliper>` instances speak their own state via the existing `.gloss` ("Measured; source given." / "Self-reported figure." / "Not measurable; reason given."). Column 3 carries a visually-hidden sentence: "An illustration of a proficiency bar, the device this card replaces. It is not a claim about any capability on this page." DOM order is column-major — traceable, then limited, then not-traceable — so the evidence is read before either gap. No `role="status"` is added, protecting TC-SKILL-07's count of 1.
coherence:
Placement: it does not sit inside `.header` (whose `max-width: 56rem` would crush it). `

` is deleted and `skillsContent.lede` retired; `.header` keeps kicker + title with its `margin-bottom` cut from `clamp(2.5rem,6vh,3.5rem)` to `clamp(1.5rem,3.5vh,2rem)`. The figure becomes a sibling between `

` and `` at full `.inner` width, carrying the displaced bottom margin. The lede's three sentences are absorbed: sentence 1 becomes the drawing, sentence 2 becomes the apex, sentence 3 becomes column 3. Extends: the Caliper's three states, used once each in their structurally correct roles — `self-reported` on his own CV, `sourced` on the one independently checkable rung, `open` on the honest break. The 45° hatch and the 3px/6px dash pitch are lifted verbatim from `Caliper.module.css`, so no new mark and no new hex enter the site. The one-shot `drawn`/`settled` IntersectionObserver and the `--i` stagger custom property are the Bench's own idiom. Avoids: no circles, bezels, dials or radial anything (About's Compass); no horizontal proportional bars on a shared axis, no gridlines or decade ticks (Experience) — the one bar-like object is deliberately drawn as the discredited thing, in construction-line inks, with its length declared arbitrary; no boxes, arrowheads or left-to-right process flow (Vitrine's drawings); no wires, curves, node-link graph or rails (the Bench itself — this is one claim in depth where the Bench is 13×17 in breadth, and the figcaption says so). Vertical ladders with a shared apex are unclaimed on this site. Gold: exactly one occurrence in the whole figure — the closed jaws of `` around `ANZ Banking Group`, the single rung a stranger can verify without taking his word for it. Not the stiles, not the ticks, not the apex, not the status glyphs, not the bar. It is a terminator, never a path. Because it is rendered by the existing component, the figure declares no new gold and adds zero risk to TC-NFR-MONO. Every string is derived: `cvFingerprint.short`/`.bytes`, and `capabilities.find(...)` for the telemetry row and the single `pending` row. The only new authored data is a `SourceKind → verification instrument` map beside `statusLegend` ("programme · verified by asking the employer" / "repository · open it now" / "credential · check with the issuer"), which serves the two audiences directly.
risks: Three ladders of mono type is dense. If the rung sub-lines run long the figure stops being a 3-second glance and becomes a second block of prose in disguise — the failure the section already has. Sub-lines must be capped at ~46 characters and the R2 reading must be the only place digits appear.

At 390px, stacked, the cross-column comparison that does all the teaching is destroyed; the reader sees three ladders in sequence, not a triad. The narrow strap admits this, but a mobile visitor gets a weaker argument than a desktop one, and no amount of CSS fixes that.

Column 3 could be screenshotted or read alone and mistaken for a real claim about Vikram, since it carries a real capability string above a bar. The visually-hidden disclaimer protects assistive tech; a sighted reader who crops the image is not protected.

'R1 · STANDARD / R2 · READING / R3 · RESULT' may read as invented jargon rather than as metrology. If it does, it costs the reader their one unit of learning budget on nomenclature instead of on the chain.

Adjacency to the Bench is the real danger: both objects are about sources, in the same section, forty pixels apart. If the figcaption does not draw the distinction (one claim in depth vs. thirteen sources in breadth) the two will read as the same diagram drawn twice, and the weaker one will be the new one.
whyBest:
It draws the *reason* a certificate means anything rather than its ornament. A stamped-paper illustration, a vernier, a dial or a guard band all say "this is instrumenty"; only the chain says what is actually being claimed — that there is something independent above this row, and here it is, and here is how you reach it. That is the site's prime directive rendered as geometry.

It is the only candidate that contains the object it refutes. The reader arrives with a proficiency-bar schema, and a schema is displaced by comparison, not by assertion — so the bar is present, in construction-line greys, with two printed dashes where the other two ladders have a source and a reading, hanging from a rule that is dashed because there is nothing real up there. Answering "why not bars" costs zero prose.

It is the only candidate where the three-state Caliper falls out structurally instead of being illustrated. Self-reported on his own CV, sourced on the one third-party-checkable rung, open on the honest break — each state appears exactly once, in the only place it could correctly go, and a reader who has never met the mark learns all three from their positions. Gold appears once, on the one thing a stranger can verify, which is the rule the site most needs taught.

It is the cheapest and safest to build. No SVG at all, so the `#skills svg path` count tests survive untouched; no measurement, so no CLS and no `useLayoutEffect`; no new colour, no new mark, no new dependency; one new motion token on an approved prefix. Its settled frame is its base stylesheet, so reduced-motion and no-JS are the canonical image rather than a fallback.

And it turns the section's weakest asset into its strongest: the CV fingerprint, currently a dead line in the footer, becomes the apex every chain hangs from — a hash the reader can run themselves.
